instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F/220°C with a rack in the middle.
Wipe the caps clean with a damp paper towel and twist out the stems. Finely chop the stems and set them aside.
Set the caps gill side up on a rimmed baking sheet. Rub them with 2 tbsp of the olive oil and sprinkle 1/4 tsp of the salt over them.
Meanwhile, put the pine nuts in a large dry skillet over medium heat. Stir for about 2 minutes, until golden and toasty. Transfer them to a small bowl.
Return the skillet to medium heat. Add the last 1 tbsp of oil and the chopped stems and cook for 3 minutes, until browned. Mince the garlic, add it and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the spinach a handful at a time and stir until it has wilted, about 2 minutes. Transfer it to a bowl and press it with the back of a spoon to push out the water. Pour off the liquid.
Stir the ricotta, 1/4 cup of the Parmesan, the oregano, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper into the spinach.
Take the caps out of the oven and pour off any liquid that has collected in them. Spoon 1/4 cup of the marinara into each cap, then divide the spinach filling among them.
Top the caps with the mozzarella, then the remaining 1/4 cup Parmesan, then the pine nuts.
Bake for 15 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling and golden in spots.
Taste a bit of the filling from one cap. If it's flat, add a pinch of salt to the rest.
Serve one cap to each person.
method_notes: The sources agree on portobello caps roasted first to release their water, then filled with spinach, ricotta and Parmesan and baked at 375 to 425°F. They differ on breadcrumbs, mozzarella, an egg, and whether marinara goes underneath. This follows the lead's pre-roast, drops the breadcrumbs for gluten-free and uses toasted pine nuts on top for crunch. Marinara goes inside the caps, as in the American Cancer Society version. Check the marinara label for gluten-free.
